purpose: Assesses whether the organization provides appropriate information to users, regulators, and other interested parties about its AI systems, including documentation, incident communication, and general transparency.
summary: This objective requires the organization to provide clear information to interested parties throughout an AI system's life cycle, including user-facing documentation, external reporting where required, communication in the event of AI-related incidents, and general information that helps interested parties understand the system's capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use.
expectedStatementElements: What user-facing documentation exists explaining an AI system's capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use
How external regulatory or compliance reporting obligations related to AI systems are tracked and fulfilled
What communication plan or process exists for notifying affected parties in the event of an AI-related incident
How the organization determines what information different interested parties (users, regulators, auditors) need and ensures it's provided
evidenceExamples: User-facing documentation (e.g., model cards, usage guidelines) for in-scope AI systems
Regulatory reporting log or tracker showing obligations and fulfillment status
Incident communication plan/template specific to AI-related incidents
Stakeholder information-needs mapping showing what's provided to whom
commonGaps: AI systems are deployed with no user-facing documentation explaining limitations or appropriate use
Regulatory reporting obligations related to AI aren't tracked, risking missed or late filings
There's no defined communication plan for notifying affected users if an AI system causes harm or malfunctions
Different interested parties (users vs. regulators vs. auditors) are given the same generic information regardless of what they actually need
interviewQuestions: If a user wanted to understand what our AI system can and can't do, is there documentation for that?
Do we track what regulatory reporting we owe related to our AI systems, and are we current on it?
If an AI system caused a real problem for users, do we have a plan for how and when we'd tell them?
Do we tailor what information we give to users versus regulators versus auditors, or send everyone the same thing?
